docs.pressable.component: `Pressable` says an element answers a finger, and declares what it WEARS while one is near it.
It is the look and the depth — never the meaning. What a press DOES is `Valued`, read by
whoever handles it, exactly as a willing zone's legality is not in `Inviting`.
```ts
import { node, Bounded, Pressable, Valued, rect } from "game-kit"
const undo = node("undo",
Bounded({ bounds: rect(1.6, 0.6) }),
Pressable(),                        // the stock feel: a wash, a sink, a nudge
Valued({ values: { does: "undo" } }))   // what a press MEANS — data, never an id to parse
## The two siblings
`Inviting` dresses a zone while a drag it would take is in flight. `Pressable` dresses a control
while a pointer is over it or down on it. Both put their coat into `Coated.self`, both hand back
an undo that restores what stood there — so a control already wearing its own coat (a toggle that
is on, a tile mid-load) keeps it when the pointer leaves — and neither leaves a `hovered` flag in
the tree for two systems to disagree about.
## Depth and displacement are two fields
`sink` is written to `z`: the plan shortens the cast shadow from it (`base + perZ * z`), so a
held control loses the height its shadow was reporting. `nudge` moves the plate itself. They are
separate because they say different things, and a design may want either alone — a flat control
with only a nudge, a floating one that only descends.
## There is no `disabled`
Capability is by presence, restriction by absence. A control that must not act is one the
consumer does not act on: the press still reports, the handler declines, and the greyed look is
an ordinary coat. A flag here would be a second source of truth about the same refusal — and the
day the two disagreed, the button would light up and do nothing.
docs.pressable.control: Three controls on one desk, all the same assembly. Move the pointer over them to see `hover`,
hold one to see `held`, `sink` and `nudge` at once. The right-hand one declares no `Valued`, so
it lights and sinks and reports nothing — a control with nothing to say is still a control.
